tasks.title: Actions: done, clear, reject, defer
tasks.goal: From a selected task: `d` marks an in_progress task done (optional changelog line), `c` clears a needs_human_look task to done (look-clear), `x` rejects it back to pending (look-clear --reject), `l` defers an in_progress task to the human queue with a note (look-defer). phases.title: Rust core
phases.goal: Move the TideTable core (todo model, scheduling, claims, validation, locking) into Rust so tidetable-tui and embedders such as Oarlock no longer need a Python install, while tkrun.py stays Python. docs/rust-port.md is the contract: six commands, exact JSON shapes, exit codes, refusal wording, and graded parity. Nothing here changes scheduling semantics; if a task would, it does not belong in this phase.

tasks.title: Core crate, storage semantics and locking
tasks.goal: New crates/tidetable-core, no GPUI and no printing: the task and phase model, load, atomic write, the append-only event log, and FileLock. Reuse tidetable/schema/todo-v1.schema.json verbatim rather than re-specifying the format. Reproduce the lock exactly: JSON payload with pid, host and at; stale when the pid is positively dead on this host or the file is older than 300s and liveness is unknown; exclusive create; 10s timeout polling every 50ms. The Windows liveness probe must return alive, dead or unknown using OpenProcess with PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION, never a signal probe, because os.kill(pid, 0) terminates the process there. do not copy the unguarded unlink in FileLock.__exit__: treat already-gone and still-open alike. Writes rename with retry, as jsonio.write_json does, because Windows refuses a rename over an open file.
success: Loading and saving a todo file round-trips it byte-identically apart from reordering
Two processes racing for the lock: exactly one wins, the loser waits or times out cleanly, and no traceback escapes
A stale lock from a dead pid is broken and the reason is reported
Atomic write succeeds while another process holds the target open

tasks.title: Scheduling, conflicts and the read commands
tasks.goal: Port the pure logic from cli.py onto the core crate: iteration and id ordering, blockers_for, ready_tasks, in_progress_tasks, find_next with resume and disjoint, blocked_report, phase_is_complete, complete_phase_ids, norm_path, paths_conflict, overlapping_paths, disjoint_tasks. Then the commands that only read: ready, next, list, deps, parallel, history. Match the JSON shapes in docs/rust-port.md section 3 exactly, including the two traps: ready and next exit 1 when nothing is runnable, which means no work rather than broken; and task_summary overwrites a task own agent with the resolved tier and adds agent_derived. list trims its tasks to id, title and status while ready does not.

tasks.title: Mutation commands and claim semantics
tasks.goal: Port start, done, look-defer, look-queue, look-clear, reset and status, plus add and add-phase, under the lock. This is the slice TKRun depends on, so the semantics are the contract: start re-run by the same owner returns 0 with refreshed true; start refuses a live lease held by another owner; done on an already-done task returns 0; done and start refuse unmet prerequisites without --force; look-defer releases the claim and counts as done for dependencies. Keep the refusal wording from docs/rust-port.md byte-identical, including that start says blocked by where done says has unmet prerequisites, because TKRun writes both into .tkrun/log.md. Keep the mutation output lines too, notably the look-defer success line.

The human text of sidebar and the markdown of convert need structural parity only: keep the section set and the width budget that tests/test_sidebar.py asserts, and keep convert section headings and the per-phase per-task structure so generated docs do not churn in diffs. Do not assert byte equality on either.

One fixture per state: empty, all done, one ready, blocked by a task, blocked by a phase, in progress held by another owner, expired lease, needs_human_look queued, cancelled prerequisite, cycle, duplicate id, missing required field. Refusals need fixtures as much as happy paths. Include the concurrency fixture: two start calls racing one task, exactly one wins, the other exits 1, and it must run on Windows.
